issue.title: Redline's last message after a response-target delivery can be its cleanup note, so the caller's reply holds no text

labels.name: needs-info
labels.description: Waiting on reporter for more information

issue.body:
> *This was generated by AI while building #480.*

Measured while building #480 and filed from its exit.

## What was measured

In `pre-article-unnamed-2`, a response-target Redline run staged from `fb169087`, the Harness returned this as the whole reply: *Inga filer har skrivits eller ändrats. `input.md` är orörd och de tillfälliga arbetsfilerna är borttagna.* That is the run's `response.txt`. The run's transcript shows that it reviewed and corrected the text. It then wrote its full delivery as a text block: the corrected text in a fenced block, its findings, its claim account and its anatomy remarks. After that block it made one more tool call to remove its scratch files, and then wrote the one-line cleanup note as its last message. A caller who reads the final reply, as `claude --print` and every Agent SDK consumer do, gets the cleanup note and no text at all.

Step 11 says that on a response target the run removes its scratch *and base[s] the delivery account on the filesystem state that remains after cleanup*. It does not say that the delivery is the run's last message. Both blind judges fail `R1` and `C1`, because the reply they were given delivers no text and reports no finding. One run of the fourteen in that arm did this, and none of the other forty-one runs in the evaluation did.

## Where it was measured

`docs/evaluation/editorial-480/runs/pre-article-unnamed-2/`, with both judgements. The transcript is not committed. `results.md` quotes it.

## Why it is filed

The protocol files every miss as its own issue naming the ticket. This miss is outside #480's target, and no open ticket carries it.

comments.body:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Make Redline's complete response-target delivery the terminal reply the caller actually receives.

## What to build

Diagnose and repair the delivery ordering that lets a cleanup-only final message replace the Text Artifact and report. Finish run-owned tools, permitted cleanup, inventory accounting, final measurement and reply checking before sending the terminal delivery. A changed text, or an unchanged text with unresolved findings, reaches the caller in one complete final reply: the artifact in its required fence and the applicable findings/claim account beside it. A genuine clean no-change run keeps the short status. Cleanup failure is reported with the actual retained paths, without concealing the text or falsely asserting cleanup success. Preserve the reply-check freeze: do not reword or supplement checked statements about the text during final assembly.

**Verification and redundancy check:** Read Redline's delivery step, reply-check contract, shared delivery contract and the fenced-response decision. They require complete delivery and accounting after cleanup but do not explicitly establish the terminal-message boundary. In #480's `pre-article-unnamed-2`, preserved `response.txt` contains only the cleanup line. The trace index shows a reply-check delegation and a later cleanup call. The committed results describe the earlier full delivery followed by that call and the cleanup-only last message; the full transcript itself is not preserved, so this triage does not claim to have inspected it. The judge confirms no artifact or finding in the caller's reply. #477's later freeze governs wording, not this ordering; test the current product before adding wording. No `.out-of-scope/` KB or relevant rejection was found.

**Key interfaces:** Redline's final delivery step, run-owned cleanup and the existing one-shot reply check; the Harness's terminal assistant reply as consumed by a non-interactive caller. Keep the change local to Redline unless diagnosis establishes an actual shared-contract gap; do not extend it to other Skills on inference alone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Commit a frozen native regression plan before runs, following the evaluation protocol and #476/#480's trace, packet, inventory and void-handling methods. Use fresh pre-change/candidate arms on one provider-native seat.
- [ ] Target the #480 `article-unnamed` input with three response runs per arm, plus three response runs on an existing flawed editorial control that normally needs correction. Keep one `article-clean` response/file pair and one distinct file-target flawed run as controls. Freeze inputs and criteria before running and record whether each targeted run actually corrected text or retained findings.
- [ ] Judge delivery from the terminal reply returned by the Harness, not an earlier stream block or the run's input file. Read the native trace separately for correction, checker completion, cleanup and final-message order. Preserve both forms of evidence and disclose any unavailable trace detail.
- [ ] In reproduced candidate cases, the terminal reply carries the whole final artifact, frontmatter intact, in one fence with its applicable report. It is not replaced by a cleanup note; no further run-owned tool call follows that terminal delivery. A clean no-change status is still valid only where the contract permits it, and a file-target reply reports the destination without duplicating the artifact.
- [ ] Cleanup/refusal accounting agrees with the inventory, refused removals are not worked around, sources remain unchanged, and the one-shot reply check and final mechanical pass are preserved. Unfaulted checked text statements are delivered word for word.
- [ ] Make product wording conditional on a fresh baseline reproduction. If it does not reproduce, preserve and report that result with no speculative wording change. Otherwise use the protocol's bounded revise/ship rules, record every remaining miss and file it; do not reinterpret a missing delivery as a successful no-change review.
- [ ] Regenerate the catalog after shipped-file changes and pass the four project checks in CONTRIBUTING.md.

**Out of scope:** Changing Harness/SDK semantics, sending files instead of a requested response, other Skills' delivery lifecycle, and repair of unrelated editorial findings encountered in the runs.
